title: Vegetation greenness did not carry the weak climate tracking of US breeding birds: birds followed 8-15% of greenness gradients, and greenness held 9% of their temperature signal (BBS, NDVI, 1985-2021)
abstract: Question: North American bird communities follow only 5-14% of their spatial temperature associations in time. Is this gap inherited from vegetation, which follows climate slowly? Data: 2,922 contiguous-US Breeding Bird Survey routes (68,130 standard runs, 1985-2021), PKU GIMMS NDVI v1.2 May-July greenness, nClimGrid climate, LCMAP land cover, AVONET habitat. Method: for 381 species, cross-fitted spatial Poisson models with climate, land cover and NDVI gave predicted log abundance per run; conditional Poisson panels with route x observer and year effects gave the transfer ratio theta (temporal response / spatial prediction; 1 = full transfer). The same design gave the transfer of route NDVI and land cover to climate. We corrected for errors in the spatial coefficients and used a 9-block year jackknife. Results: route greenness followed 0.35 (jackknife 0.26-0.44) of its spatial 5-year temperature prediction and 0.17 of its rain prediction; land-cover classes followed climate at about 0. Birds followed their 5-year greenness association at 0.081 (0.063-0.098; corrected 0.15) and same-year greenness at only 0.013 (corrected 0.024). NDVI carried 9% and land cover plus NDVI 19% of the within-route temperature signal. The chain predicted a corrected temperature transfer of 0.083 (observed 0.075); full vegetation and land-cover tracking of climate would raise it only to 0.11, and perfect habitat tracking by birds to 0.27. Transfer grew with the averaging window (temperature 0.010, 0.050, 0.082 for 1, 5, 10 years) but stayed small. Grassland and human-modified-habitat birds followed greenness at 0.33-0.34 (corrected), forest birds at 0.07. Conclusion: weak space-for-time transfer occurs at every link, also for vegetation itself and for a direct resource variable, but vegetation lag is not the main cause of the bird gap: most of the gap is in the direct temperature association. Limitations: 9 km NDVI is a coarse habitat proxy; mediation shares assume habitat is on the causal path; the chain, climate-only model and time-scale checks were added after the main fits; correlational design.
